text: A light wave is incident normally on a glass slab of refractive index 1.5. If 4 % of light gets reflected and the amplitude of the electric field of the incident light is 30 V/m, then the amplitude of the electric field for the wave propagating in the glass medium will be :

solution.body:
In a medium of refractive index $n$ the intensity is $I=\dfrac{1}{2}nε_{0}cE_{0}^{2}$, so $I\propto nE_{0}^{2}$.

With $4%$ reflected, $96%$ of the incident intensity enters the glass ($n=1.5$) from air ($n=1$):

$1.5E_{t}^{2}=0.96\times (30)^{2}$

$E_{t}^{2}=\dfrac{0.96}{1.5}\times 900=0.64\times 900=576\Rightarrow E_{t}=24\text{V m}^{-1}$

Hence, the correct option is (D).

text: Let the moment of inertia of a hollow cylinder of length 30 cm (inner radius 10 cm and outer radius 20 cm), about its axis be I. The radius of a thin cylinder of the same mass such that its moment of inertia about its axis is also I, is :

solution.body:
Consider an element of radius x and thickness dx

Mass of element, dm = $σ2πx(dx)$

Here, $σ$ = mass per unit area = $\frac{m}{π(R^{2}-r^{2})}$

Moment of inertia of element, $dI = (dm)x^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ I = $σ2π\int\limits _{r}^{R}x^{3}dx$

= $σ2π\left (\frac{R^{4}-r^{4}}{4}\right )$

Moment of inertia of thin cylinder of same mass,

$\Rightarrow$ m$r_{0}^{2}$ = $\frac{m}{2}\left (R^{2}+r^{2}\right )$

$\Rightarrow$ $r_{0}^{2}$ = 250

$\Rightarrow$ $r_{0}$ $\simeq$ 16 cm

text:
A point source of light, S is placed at distance L in front of the centre of plane mirror of width d which is hanging vertically on a wall. sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
The image $S^{'}$ of the source lies a distance $L$ behind the mirror, opposite its centre.

Reflected light reaches the man only along lines that start at $S^{'}$ and pass through the mirror. The two lines from $S^{'}$ through the edges of the mirror (width $d$, at distance $L$ from $S^{'}$) spread out until they meet the man's path, which is $L+2L=3L$ from $S^{'}$.

By similar triangles, the length of the man's path inside this region is

$d\times \dfrac{3L}{L}=3d$

Hence, the correct option is (C).

text:
A simple pendulum, made of a string of length $\ell$ and a bob of mass m, is released from a small angle $θ_{0}$. It strikes a block of mass M, kept on a horizontal surface at its lowest point of oscillations, elastically. It
bounces back and goes up to an angle $θ_{1}$. Then M is given by :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
[IMG]


v = $\sqrt{2g\ell (1-\cos θ_{0})}$

$v_{1} =$ $\sqrt{2g\ell (1-\cos θ_{1})}$

By momentum conservation

m$\sqrt{2gl(1-\cos θ_{0})}$
$=MV_{m}-m\sqrt{2g\ell (1-\cos θ_{1})}$

$\Rightarrowm\sqrt{2g\ell }\left \{\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}+\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}\right \}$

$=$ $MV_{m}$

and  e = 1 = $\frac{V_{m}+\sqrt{2g\ell (1-\cos θ_{1})}}{\sqrt{2g\ell (1-\cos θ_{0})}}$

$\sqrt{2g\ell }$ $\left (\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}-\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}\right )$
$=$ $V_{m}$     . . .(I)

m$\sqrt{2g\ell }\left (\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}+\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}\right )$
$=$ $MV_{M}$     . . .(II)

Dividing 

$\frac{\left (\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}+\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}\right )}{\left (\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}-\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}\right )}=\frac{M}{m}$

By componendo and dividendo

$\frac{M-m}{M+m}$ = $\frac{\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{1}}}{\sqrt{1-\cos θ_{0}}}=\frac{\sin \left (\frac{θ1}{2}\right )}{\sin \left (\frac{θ0}{2}\right )}$

$\Rightarrow$  $\frac{M}{m}=\frac{θ_{0}+θ_{1}}{θ_{0}-θ_{1}}\Rightarrow M=m\left (\frac{θ_{0}+θ_{1}}{θ_{0}-θ_{1}}\right )$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot

In a meter bridge, the wire of length 1 m has a non-uniform cross-section such that, the variation $\frac{dR}{d\ell }$ of its resistance R with length $\ell$  is $\frac{dR}{d\ell }$ $\propto$ $\frac{1}{\sqrt{\ell }}$. Two equal resistances are connected as shown in the figure. The

solution.body:

where C = constant.

AP is $R_{1}$ and PB is $R_{2}$

$\therefore$  $\frac{R^{'}}{R^{'}}=\frac{R_{1}}{R_{2}}$   or    $R_{1} = R_{2}$

Now    $\int dR=c\int \frac{d\ell }{\sqrt{\ell }}$

Putting $R_{1} = R_{2}$

C2$\sqrt{\ell }$ = C(2 $-$ 2$\sqrt{\ell }$)

$\Rightarrow$   $f=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{\frac{C}{1}}=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{\frac{\frac{K\ell 2}{2}}{\frac{M\ell 2}{12}}}$

$\Rightarrow$    $f=\frac{1}{2π}\sqrt{\frac{6K}{M}}$

text:
A particle of mass m moves in a circular orbit in a central potential field U(r) = $\frac{1}{2}$ $kr^{2}$. If Bohr 's
quantization conditions are applied, radii of possible orbitls and energy levels vary with quantum number n as :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2019 (Online) 12th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Force due to this field, F = $-\frac{𝜕U}{𝜕r}$

F = $-\frac{𝜕}{𝜕r}\left (\frac{1}{2}kr^{2}\right )$ = -kr

For circular orbit, $\frac{mv^{2}}{r}$ = -kr

$\Rightarrow$ v $\propto$ r ..... (1)

Fron Bohr’s quantization condition

mvr = $\frac{nh}{2π}$ .....(2)

From (1) and (2),

$r_{n}$ $\propto$ $n^{\frac{1}{2}}$

Given, U(r) = $\frac{1}{2}kr^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{n} =$ $-\frac{1}{2}U(r)$ = $-\frac{1}{4}kr^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $E_{n}$ $\propto$ n
